newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EMU bond market likely to develop quickly - EMI head.
newsitem.headline: EMU bond market likely to develop quickly - EMI head.

text.p: A bond market denominated in a single European currency is likely to develop rapidly after the start of economic and monetary union, Alexandre Lamfalussy, President of the European Monetary Institute, said on Thursday.

Speaking at a dinner sponsored by the American Chamber of Commerce in Belgium, Lamfalussy said finance ministries throughout Europe were working on the nuts and bolts of such a market and it would likely "happen more quickly than one would normally expect."
A key element in building the bond market would be the rapid redenomination of the outstanding national debt of the governments participating in EMU, Lamfalussy added.
"My own guess is that the process of redenomination in euros will be very fast and will be triggered by competitive pressure," he told the grouping of bankers and industrialists.

France and Belgium have already announced they would convert existing national debt into the common currency at the start date, expected on January 1, 1999. Germany has yet to announce whether or not it would follow such a strategy.

Lamfalussy forecast that the creation of such a market would in turn lead to more balanced relations among the world's major currencies and could prompt a reconsideration of what the global currency market would look like.

Regarding the future credibility of a European Central Bank, the EMI chief said the mandate of such an institution towards achieving price stability ruled out the possiblity of political interference.
Moreover, with virtually all EU central banks currently committed to such an objective, he could see no reason why the future ECB would follow a different policy approach.
